If you use the free “Everything” search app (voidtools), Dogfile can ask it for results, so searches across whole drives come back instantly. It needs Everything running plus its small command-line tool es.exe (download “ES” from voidtools.com and put es.exe next to Everything.exe, portable copies included). Settings > Tools > Use Everything shows whether it’s ready. Dogfile’s own instant index (Settings > Search) does the same job without Everything.

n: Dialog jump (Ctrl+G in Open / Save dialogs)
q: dialog jump save open dialog another program ctrl+g jump current folder
h: In any program’s Open or Save dialog, press Ctrl+G: a menu lists the folders open in Dogfile (the one you’re in first), plus Desktop, Documents and Downloads. Pick one and the dialog goes straight there. Settings > Behavior > Dialog jump turns it on or off, and can also make every Open / Save dialog start in your current Dogfile folder by itself. It works in the standard Windows dialogs of every program; restart Dogfile after changing it.

n: Shortcuts: select by pattern, Drop Shelf
q: keyboard shortcut select files by pattern drop shelf open shelf keys
h: Select by pattern: Ctrl+Shift+A (or + on the number pad) — type *.jpg;*.png, or /regex/ for a regular expression. Drop Shelf: Ctrl+Shift+J shows or hides it, Ctrl+Alt+J puts the selected files on it. Every shortcut is listed (and can be changed) in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts, and the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) shows each command’s keys.

n: Why a copy failed, and retrying only the failed files
q: why did my file copy fail retry failed files operations queue error problems
h: Open the Operations panel (the button in the status bar that shows running copies). A finished job lists each file that failed and why in plain words — in use by another program (use “What’s locking this?”), access denied, the destination is full, the path is too long, or the network dropped. Fix the cause, then press “Retry failed”: only the files that failed are copied again. File history (Ctrl+Shift+H) keeps the same list with a Retry button later on.

n: Dogfile Player for .mkv, and Dogfile as the Windows file manager
q: default app mkv player video default file manager win+e explorer replace
h: Inside Dogfile: Settings > Tools & apps > File types — set .mkv (or any type) to Dogfile Player; right-click a file > Open with > “Always open .mkv files with” does the same. For Windows itself, the File types list has “Set the Windows default…”, which opens Windows’ own chooser for that type. To replace File Explorer: Settings > General > Default file manager > Make Dogfile the default — Win+E, folder shortcuts and “Show in folder” then open Dogfile, and the same place puts File Explorer back.

h: Settings > Appearance > Glass sidebar, the View ribbon’s “Glass sidebar” button, or right-click the sidebar. The sidebar turns translucent with a frosted blur; on Windows 10/11 the desktop shows through it (after opening a new window or restarting Dogfile once).

n: Buying Pro and entering a serial number
h: Click Get Pro (top right) or Settings > Licence > Buy now. Payment is by Stripe in your browser; Dogfile activates itself as soon as it goes through, and your serial number (DOGF-XXXXX-…) is on your Stripe receipt and emailed to you. On another PC choose Settings > Licence > Enter serial number. One serial number works on 2 PCs.
q: buy serial number licence license key activate purchase receipt

n: Moving Pro to another PC, or activating offline
h: A serial number works on 2 PCs at a time. To move it, open Dogfile on the old PC and choose Settings > Licence > Deactivate this PC, then enter the serial number on the new one. For a PC without internet, choose Settings > Licence > Activate offline: open the link it shows on a phone or another computer, and type the activation code it gives you back into Dogfile (or save it as a file and open it).
q: move licence another pc deactivate offline activation no internet new computer
